engagement_title: SentinelMesh launch quarter: cut a self-recorded platform demo into a highlight and two strictly shorter cuts, bring five room photographs and a lost mark to one enterprise identity, and hand back caption cards the client can re-clear every quarter
vertical: Technology, SaaS and startups. Enterprise human-cyber-risk platform sold on annual contracts to CISOs and IT directors (Denver, Colorado), going out across website, sales calls, webinars, investor conversations and social in one quarter
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, seeking an 'experienced video editor and motion graphics designer to create a polished marketing and product demonstration video for our AI-powered cybersecurity platform', a product that 'helps organizations reduce human cyber risk through a combination of real-time protection, adaptive simulations, and in-the-moment learning', with the finished pieces running on 'website, sales presentations, webinars, investor discussions, and social media' and the deliverable list pinned at one 90 to 120 second master, one 30 second cutdown and one 15 second teaser. The real company names no client publicly, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional SentinelMesh. That posted job is written as if the video were the whole commission, which is what made the earlier version of this task sit on one surface. The fuller commission the same client genuinely needs is the one the post's own distribution list implies: the same identity has to survive on the website hero stills, in the sales deck, on the social cards and on the dark ground the platform's own interface uses, from source material the founders recorded themselves. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that honest, because HTML authoring now returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, which is exactly the 're-cleared every quarter' artefact this buyer needs and the posted brief never thought to ask for.
client_one_liner: Our head of product recorded the demo himself, the three moments the whole pitch rests on are buried somewhere in twenty two minutes of screen capture, our five product photographs were shot by five different people, and we go out in six weeks.
client_brief:
SentinelMesh, launch quarter

We are a Denver security software company. Our platform reduces human cyber risk: it watches for the risky moment, runs an adaptive simulation, and coaches the person on the spot. We sell to CISOs and IT directors on annual contracts, and in six weeks the platform goes out on our website, in the sales deck, on webinars, in investor conversations and on social.

What we have. Our head of product recorded the product himself, three screen recordings of the platform in use plus two clips of the office. Somewhere in the long recording are the three things the whole pitch rests on: the risk score resolving, the simulation firing, and the coaching card appearing. All three have to be in the finished piece, and a technical buyer has to be able to read the screen while they are on it.

He also recorded the voice over, across two sittings in the glass meeting room. It is understandable but it wanders.

We need one demo piece of about a minute and a half, a thirty second cut for sales calls and a fifteen second teaser, and the short ones have to be genuinely cut down from the long piece rather than separate edits. We need the teaser upright for phones as well.

Five photographs of the platform running in real rooms, all shot by different people on different days. They need to look like one company.

Our logo exists as an export and as a photograph of our trade show banner, and neither is the file our designer made. We need it back as artwork we can put on a dark ground.

And caption cards for the claims in our messaging sheet, in a file we can edit ourselves, because the claims get re-cleared every quarter.

Contracts run forty to ninety thousand a year. It has to look like something you can trust. Plus a note on what you did.
price_band_and_audience: Enterprise security software at forty to ninety thousand dollars a year, bought by a CISO or IT director with a security engineer reading over their shoulder. The band is load-bearing: at this price the whole treatment has to be restrained, precise and quiet, with the product interface legible at the size a buyer actually watches it, muted neutrals against the platform's own dark navy, one accent, and claims that read as cleared rather than sold. The same platform pitched at a nineteen dollar a seat self-serve band would correctly be fast, bright, heavily captioned and cut for thumb-stopping, and shipping that here reads as a consumer app and costs the technical buyer's trust in the first five seconds. Push the other way into slow abstract corporate atmosphere with the interface never legible and it reads as a company that will not show its product, which is fatal in security specifically. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Catch the risky moment. Coach it away.
brand_identity.sector: Enterprise cybersecurity software (human cyber risk platform, SaaS)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022 in Denver, Colorado. Roughly 40 people, venture-backed, entering its first full launch quarter.
brand_identity.about: SentinelMesh reduces human cyber risk for regulated enterprises. The platform watches for the risky moment, runs an adaptive simulation, and coaches the person in real time, closing the gap between security policy and daily behavior. We sell to CISOs and IT directors on annual contracts and we win on trust, precision, and proof that the product does what we say.
brand_identity.audience: CISOs, IT directors, and the security engineers reading over their shoulder at mid-market and enterprise organizations. Technical, skeptical, and short on patience for hype.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Premium enterprise. Annual contracts from 40,000 to 90,000 dollars. Everything we ship has to read as a considered purchase a security leader can defend internally, never as a self-serve consumer app.
brand_identity.typography: A single humanist sans family across headings and body, set with generous spacing and modest weight contrast. No display faces, no condensed heads. Numerals and interface labels stay legible at the size a buyer actually reads them.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, exact, and calm. We state what the product does and let it read as cleared rather than sold. We avoid fear language, exclamation, and buzzwords. One accent, one idea per line.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our designer built the original identity and left the company, and that working file left with him. What survives is a flat export of the mark on white and a phone photo of our trade show banner, neither of which is the source artwork. The mark needs to be rebuilt as usable artwork that sits correctly on our dark navy ground.
brand_identity.values: Trust earned through evidence, restraint over spectacle, clarity for a technical buyer, and claims that are cleared before they are spoken.

assets_supplied.name: sentinelmesh_demo_raw/ (3 screen recordings, longest 22 minutes, plus 2 office b-roll clips)
assets_supplied.kind: Self-recorded product capture and office b-roll, shot by the head of product over one afternoon, with an unscripted cursor and no marked in and out points.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything he recorded. The three moments are in the long one somewhere, he did not write down where."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The three moments the pitch rests on are the quietest stretches in the whole recording: the risk score resolves over several seconds of an almost static dashboard, and the coaching card appears with nothing else on screen moving, while the opening hero animation and the navigation churn are the motion-dense parts. Separately one office b-roll clip carries a 4K frame size but was window-captured at a much smaller size and enlarged by the recorder at export, so its real detail ceiling sits far below what its stated dimensions imply and no filename or property says so.

assets_supplied.name: sentinelmesh_vo.wav (voice over, two sittings)
assets_supplied.kind: Founder voice over recorded in a glass-walled meeting room across two sittings a week apart, at two mic distances.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "He read it twice because we changed a line. It is understandable but it wanders."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The two sittings sit at different levels and different room distances, so a single pass of speech cleaning normalises toward one of them and pushes the other forward or leaves it behind. One of the regulatory-cleared claim clauses sits underneath an HVAC swell that begins mid-sentence, so that clause survives the cleaning at a different intelligibility from every clause around it.

assets_supplied.name: sentinelmesh_stills/ (5 frames, mixed cameras)
assets_supplied.kind: Five photographs of the platform running in real rooms: a security operations desk, a wall display in a lobby, two laptop-on-desk shots and one over-shoulder in a meeting room. Five photographers, five days.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Five rooms, five different people took them. They need to look like one company."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The operations desk frame was shot with the overheads on and the monitor wall is clipped to flat white across its whole face, so a highlight recovery on it returns success while the readout is that nothing moves at all. One laptop-on-desk frame puts the screen in the outer right third, so any centre-weighted crop to a square or an upright destination cuts the product out of the picture it is supposed to prove. And the platform interface's own dark navy chrome sits close in value to two of the five rooms, so a whole-frame tonal correction that fixes the room takes the chrome off brand.

assets_supplied.name: sentinelmesh_logo/ (2 files: mark_export.png, tradeshow_banner.jpg)
assets_supplied.kind: A flat export of the mark on white, and a handheld photograph of the trade show banner with the mark printed large on matte vinyl. The mark is a shield with an enclosed lattice interior and a hairline outer rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Two logo files. Neither is the one our designer made, we lost that when he left."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The interior lattice is enclosed, so background removal returns a solid filled shield that looks perfectly clean on white and fills in completely on the dark ground the video and the cards actually use. On the banner photograph the printed ink and the matte vinyl run close in value across the lit left side, and naming the banner rather than the ink's own visual properties pulls any selection to the whole banner instead of the mark.

assets_supplied.name: sentinelmesh_messaging.csv (14 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The messaging matrix: claim, buyer persona, proof point and clearance status, as maintained by the company's counsel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The claims as cleared. These are the ones we are allowed to say."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the fourteen rows are the same claim written in two tenses, and one row carries a review flag in a status column the client never mentions in the brief, so a card set built by taking the sheet at face value ships a duplicate claim and one claim that is not actually cleared.

acceptance_bar: All three of the named moments (the risk score resolving, the simulation firing, the coaching card appearing) are present in the demo highlight, each held long enough that a technical buyer can read the screen while it is on. A highlight that is well paced and does not contain all three is a fail.

The thirty second cut and the fifteen second teaser are each genuinely shorter than the piece they came from and carry no material the longer piece does not, and the upright teaser is derived from the same cut rather than edited separately.

No delivered video or still exceeds its source in frame size, and nothing is brought up to a delivery size by enlargement. A piece that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even when it looks acceptable at a glance.
The voice over is even in level and intelligibility across the whole run, with no clause sitting noticeably forward or behind its neighbours and no cleared claim buried.

The five room photographs read as one company laid side by side: one white point, one black point, one treatment of the screens, and the platform's own dark navy chrome holding its colour in every one of them.
Any photograph whose screens cannot be brought back is named in the note rather than shipped as a blank white panel.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: a genuinely open interior lattice, a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and it still reads as the shield at the size it actually sits on the caption cards and on the dark ground.
On every caption card the words are live text we can retype in one licensed type system, and the text is actually visible on the card, on every card and not only the first one.
The caption card set is one working file carrying every card, each canvas keeping its own size, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
Every claim on a card traces to a cleared row of the messaging sheet, with no claim appearing twice and nothing uncleared shipped.

The note records, per photograph and per clip, what was applied and why, every resize any tool reported, what the cut actually kept and what it dropped, and anything we should know about using the mark.

adobe_surfaces.tools: video_create_quick_cut, video_resize, media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole motion half. It locates the three named moments inside twenty two minutes of unmarked screen capture, builds the highlight by shortening rather than assembling, derives the thirty second and fifteen second cuts as genuine reductions of their parent, re-aspects the teaser upright without ever enlarging, and cleans a voice over recorded across two sittings at two mic distances by treating the sittings separately rather than as one pass.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_apply_auto_tone, image_adjust_highlights, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision. It brings five differently shot rooms to one enterprise target while keeping the platform's own navy chrome on brand through confined rather than whole-frame corrections, triages what can and cannot be recovered on a clipped monitor wall, produces both the light-ground and the transparent variants the website band needs, and recovers the mark at ink level off a photographed banner with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The caption card set as one native editable document carrying every card, at the card sizes the sales deck and the social feed each need, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free-form fixed-canvas layout. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized wrapper so it stays vector and stays on canvas, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the caption cards and the handover. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on trustworthy enterprise rather than startup energy or defence-contractor severity. Numeric weights are non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one room the founders never photographed, a quiet enterprise operations environment at genuine camera scale, IP-clean, with generative-tech candidates excluded and the frame chosen for whether its existing light can be brought to the same target as the five. The Boards half persists the shared selects set the founders and their counsel sign off from, placed within the per-call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The cuts and the reframe are motion work, the photographs are raster work, and the caption cards have to be an authored fixed canvas document because the client re-clears the claims quarterly and nothing else in the connector composes free-form layout. The brief pins the destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which clip and which room.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Summarise the long screen recording to find where the three named moments actually sit, and summarise the two b-roll clips to know what they contain.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts the three moments are in there and does not know where. A summary is the only channel that reads twenty two minutes of unmarked capture, and reading it against the messaging sheet is what turns a located passage into a claim the piece has to prove.
trajectory.produces: A located inventory of the three named moments and a content note per b-roll clip.

trajectory.action: Clean the voice over, treating the two sittings as two passes rather than one, and check the cleaned result against the cleared claim list clause by clause.
trajectory.judgement: One pass over a file recorded at two mic distances normalises toward whichever sitting dominates. The claim clauses are the part that has to survive, so intelligibility is judged where the claims are, not on the whole file's average.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned narration bed with a per-sitting parameter log and a clause-level intelligibility note.

trajectory.action: Build the demo highlight at the length the client asked for by shortening the source, then look at what actually came back against the three named moments.
trajectory.judgement: The highlight is not an assembly, it is a reduction, and the tool decides which seconds survive. The only thing that settles whether the piece is deliverable is watching what it kept.
trajectory.produces: A demo highlight at the target length, with a written account of which of the three moments it holds and for how long.

trajectory.action: Derive the thirty second cut and then the fifteen second teaser, each strictly shorter than the piece it came from, and confirm nothing new appears in either.
trajectory.judgement: The client asked for cutdowns, not three edits. Each shorter piece has to carry the moment its audience needs, so the sales cut and the teaser are not the same thirty and fifteen seconds of the same passage.
trajectory.produces: A thirty second sales cut and a fifteen second teaser, each traceable to a passage of the highlight.

trajectory.action: Re-aspect the teaser upright for phones from the teaser itself, at or below the frame size it came back at, and check what the upright framing leaves in shot.
trajectory.judgement: The re-aspect ceiling is set by what the cut actually returned, not by the original recording, and enlarging back to a phone-native size is not an option. Upright framing on a dashboard capture decides whether the buyer still sees the thing being demonstrated.
trajectory.produces: An upright teaser at a size no larger than its source, with the reframing decision recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview all five room photographs and triage them: which illuminant, which are level, where the screens sit in the frame, and how close the platform's navy chrome runs to each room.
trajectory.judgement: The five are the only place the question of whether this is one company gets settled. Reading them as a set is a different act from opening them one at a time.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, tilt, screen placement and chrome contrast.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, then fix one enterprise target off the best lit frame and correct each of the five toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels so it cannot follow a crop, and one batched parameter set is exactly wrong for five rooms lit five ways. The agent holds one destination and reaches it by five routes.
trajectory.produces: Five graded room masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Recover what can be recovered in the bright screens, then apply confined corrections wherever a whole-frame move would take the platform's navy chrome off brand, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the laptop pulls the selection to the laptop. The chrome is the brand's own colour in the one place a buyer will read it, so it is the thing the grade has to protect.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole-frame move would have taken the chrome grey or the room muddy, plus a note on what each screen would and would not give back.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the one room the founders never photographed, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the same target as the five, not the most striking thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale frame graded into the same world as the five.

trajectory.action: Produce the website variants: the light ground plates for the site band and genuinely transparent variants where the band colour is the platform's own navy, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only channel that reports what a tool did to a frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language. A frame whose subject sits in the outer third will not survive a centre-weighted crop to a square destination.
trajectory.produces: A plate set and a transparent variant set, each with its returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark: triage the two supplied logo files, take one for the trace and the other for colour reference, word the selection at ink level, set the polarity, crop from the selection's own returned bounds, trace, then inject a viewBox and remove the opaque full canvas ground path.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: which of the two files is the trace source and which is only reference, how to word a selection so it takes the printed ink and not the vinyl, and which polarity to trace. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed lattice and will hand back a filled shield.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark with an open interior, plus a colour-accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own art direction, judged against a CISO buyer and a forty to ninety thousand dollar contract. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug, not by asking for a heavy weight.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry or designer, and the actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the messaging sheet into the card list, then author one self-contained HTML carrying every card, inlining every photograph as image data, placing the mark as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, declaring family and weight on every text element, and letting each root declare its own canvas.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how restrained the card can be and still carry a cleared claim legibly on the platform's dark ground.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the whole card set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, upload the HTML and export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at card one, and parse the returned per-card markup for every other card.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at card one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first card, and a per-card markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded rooms and the licensed frame within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success, and the vector mark is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the highlight actually kept. The cut is produced by shortening rather than by assembly, so which seconds survive is decided by the tool, and on twenty two minutes of screen capture the passages with the most frame-to-frame change are the opening hero animation and the cursor-heavy navigation, while the risk score resolving and the coaching card appearing are the quietest, most static stretches in the whole recording. The returned piece is the requested length, well paced and entirely watchable, and the loss is not that it looks broken but that the three things the entire pitch rests on may be exactly the three things it dropped. Nothing in the recording's properties, the summary, or the tool's response predicts which way it will fall.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls what a shortening pass elects to keep, so a careful agent faces the same uncertainty in whatever sequence it runs. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the three moments are in the long recording somewhere and that they have to be in the finished piece, which is the client's requirement, not a disclosure that a cutting tool prefers motion. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different route entirely: stop cutting one pass over the full recording and instead cut against source material already narrowed to each named moment, holding the three separately and letting the tool shorten within each.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan what the cut is run against: derive per-moment source material from the summary's located passages, shorten each on its own so no single pass can trade one moment against another, then re-derive the thirty second and fifteen second cuts and the upright reframe from the rebuilt highlight rather than from the first one.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A polished ninety second demo delivered to a security buyer that never shows the risk score resolving, which is the one thing the sales conversation is built to point at, with every tool response in the run having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the operations desk photograph has anything left in its screens. That frame was shot with the overheads on and the monitor wall has gone flat across its whole face, so a highlight recovery on it returns a successful call, a new file and a parameter that was genuinely applied, and the readout is that nothing moves at all. There is no error, no warning and no tradeoff entry, because the tool did exactly what was asked of it on data that has nothing left to give. Whether this is one frame or three of the five is a property of each photographer's exposure that afternoon and is not visible from a filename, a property or the frame at preview scale.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that prevents it: the only way to learn whether a bright region still holds information is to try to pull it back and look. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the five were shot by five people on five days and that they must look like one company, which is the client's requirement, not a warning that one is unrecoverable. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the answer is a different treatment for that frame: either build the shot around a region that survived, using a bounds crop driven by an explicit selection, or accept that the screens are gone, treat that room as atmosphere rather than as evidence, and put a different photograph where the proof shot was going.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-decide the role of the affected frames, re-cut what the website band and the card set are built from, re-grade the remaining set so it still reads as one company with a member removed or demoted, and name in the note the photographs whose screens could not be brought back.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A website band and a card set built on a photograph whose monitor wall is a blank white panel, shipped to a technical buyer as proof that the product exists, with the recovery step reported as successful in the run log.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the caption cards are built on. An enterprise caption card is a translucent panel that sits over the photograph with the image softened behind it and the type held off the panel by a layered shadow, and the type itself is often held in an outlined weight so it survives on both light and dark rooms. The importer discards a blur outright, keeps only the first layer of a layered shadow, drops blend modes, and turns outlined type into a colour value that is completely invisible while returning success on all four. The returned per-card markup is the only channel that reports any of it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so every card after the first can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for cards the client can edit and for claims that read, which is art direction and a requirement, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to produce a different upstream asset: bake the softened ground into the raster by preparing the photograph itself, reduce the shadow to the single layer that survives, and set the type in a real weight on a solid panel instead of an outline, then re-compose every card around those decisions.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the card ground as prepared raster rather than as a live effect, re-set the type off the outline construction, re-author the HTML around whichever survives, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every card from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A caption card set handed over as an editable file in which the claims are invisible on every card after the first, the panels are hard-edged blocks over unsoftened photographs, and the export reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: SentinelMesh demo cut set with cleaned narration
deliverables.spec: One demo highlight at the client's stated length containing all three named product moments held long enough to read the screen, one thirty second sales cut and one fifteen second teaser each genuinely shorter than the piece it derives from and traceable to a passage of it, plus one upright teaser reframed from the teaser at or below its source frame size. Carried on a narration bed cleaned per recording sitting rather than in one pass, even in level and intelligibility across every cleared claim. Delivered with a written account of what the cut kept and what it dropped.

deliverables.name: SentinelMesh room photography, five sources plus one licensed
deliverables.spec: Five room photographs brought to one enterprise target (one white point, one black point, one treatment of the screens) with the platform's own navy chrome holding its colour in every frame, plus one licensed camera-scale frame graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours, and an explicit statement of which screens could not be brought back.

deliverables.name: SentinelMesh website band plates, light ground and transparent
deliverables.spec: The site band set at the destination sizes, cut with one logic across every room: light ground plates for the pale band and genuinely transparent variants for the band that uses the platform's own navy, every output at or below its source frame dimensions with its returned tradeoff record kept. This is one set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are motion work, which are raster work, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free-form layout.
What the highlight is actually cut against: one pass over twenty two minutes of unmarked capture, or source narrowed to each named moment first.
How long each named moment has to be held for a technical buyer to read the screen, versus the pace a ninety second piece wants.
Which passage of the highlight each shorter cut takes, given that the sales call and the teaser are not persuading the same person of the same thing.
Whether the voice over is cleaned as one file or as two sittings, and where intelligibility is judged.
Which of the five rooms is the proof shot and which are atmosphere, and what happens to that decision when a room's screens turn out to be gone.
Whether a room's tonal correction runs whole-frame or is confined, given that the platform's navy chrome is the brand's colour in the one place a buyer reads it.
Which of the two supplied logo files is the trace source and which is only colour reference, and how to word a selection so it takes printed ink and not vinyl.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a CISO buyer, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How much a caption card can carry and still read as cleared rather than sold at this contract value.
How to report the duplicated claim and the flagged row without editing the client's counsel-maintained sheet on their behalf.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image or video model and it returns generic security software footage and stock-looking office photographs. IDENTITY: this is this company's actual platform interface with its actual dashboard, its actual risk score and its actual coaching card, recorded by its own head of product, and the mark has to be RECOVERED off a photographed banner rather than reinvented, because a regenerated shield is a different company's logo. SPEC: the highlight must contain three specific moments from a specific twenty two minute recording, each shorter cut must be a genuine reduction of its parent, the upright teaser must not be enlarged, and every claim must trace to a cleared row of a counsel-maintained sheet, none of which a generated piece satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the caption cards are defined by being editable, because the claims are re-cleared every quarter and the client explicitly cannot re-commission each time. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did the cut keep the risk score resolving, is there anything left in that monitor wall, did the card's panel survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is drawn from CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account) and the standing DOABLE list, five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. MOTION: video_create_quick_cut only ever SHORTENS, which is exactly why the first checkpoint is real, video_resize never enlarges, and media_summarize and media_enhance_speech are the summary and speech surfaces; these run on the connector's submit-and-resolve path and no gate in this task depends on measuring a frame or a waveform, only on watching and listening to what came back. No timestamp trimming, no format conversion and no frame extraction is used anywhere. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, auto_tone, highlight recovery, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The checkpoints rest on documented findings rather than assumptions: the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry is live, remove_background returns a SOLID OPAQUE DISC on an enclosed interior (118,823 opaque pixels where a true knockout would give about 18,000), vectorize emits no viewBox and an opaque path zero, alpha survives crops at outputFileType png, and crop_and_resize will silently interpolate up to a two times cap while reporting it only inside tradeoffs. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, filter blur is DROPPED, multi-layer box-shadow is TRUNCATED TO LAYER ONE, mix-blend-mode is dropped, and outlined type resolves to a fully transparent colour value, all at HTTP success, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returns a real camera-scale JPEG, and boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and a partial success reported as a success. AVOIDED: no animate_design, no fill_text, no video_render or video_render_frame, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.
